question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $71u+29v=\text{gcd}(71,29).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}71 & = & 29\cdot 2 & + & 13 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 29 & = & 13\cdot 2 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 13 & = & 3\cdot 4 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

  

As a result, $\text{gcd}(71,29)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13 & =71-29\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =29-13\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =13-3\cdot 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =13-3\cdot 4 \\  & =13-[29-13\cdot 2]\cdot 4 \\  & =13\cdot 9-29\cdot 4 \\  & =[71-29\cdot 2]\cdot 9-29\cdot 4 \\  & =71\cdot 9-29\cdot 22 \\  & =71\cdot 9+29\cdot (-22)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=9+(-22)=-13.
$$
